doctrine: The condition matrix is data in the repository, not arguments a runner improvises (#113). A cell names a set of levers; the empty set is the baseline, which is what production dispatches. One-thing-per-axis is the baseline discipline and it is blind to interaction, so a cell may name more than one lever and the report carries the interaction term — combined effect minus the sum of singles (#233, ADR-0018 Q2).

rules.slot: Every lever declares the one thing it writes. Two levers writing the same slot may not share a cell: the result would depend on the order they were applied, and an order-dependent cell is not a condition, it is a bug with a name. Checked when the matrix loads.
rules.stage: 'contract' levers transform the Contract before the prompt is assembled; 'message' levers transform the rendered user message and the prompt is re-costed afterwards, so the cost axis never reports the pre-ablation token count.
rules.baseline: Exactly one cell must declare no levers. Every effect in the report is measured against it, and the interaction term is undefined without it.

noscaffold.what: Removes the target's current content, so the model writes the whole file rather than completing a partial one.
noscaffold.why: #225's paired size manipulation. On a contract carrying no target_content it is a no-op by construction, so the eligible set is selected by the caller — an ineligible task contributes a concordant pair and dilutes the test. bug_fix is ineligible for a stronger reason: its target_content is the buggy file the task exists to fix, so removing it deletes the task rather than lightening it.

planonly.what: Keeps the scaffold's comment lines and drops its code.
planonly.why: noscaffold removes two things at once — the code the model would have typed, and the recipe telling it what to do. Splitting them gives two paired contrasts on the same problems: stock against planonly is the code the scaffold saved, planonly against noscaffold is the plan it stated.

norule.what: Removes the OUTPUT section — the output-shape sentence render_user_message appends from _REPLY_INSTRUCTIONS.
norule.why: #231 check 2's positive control. CLM-0017 measured this one line moving first-pass acceptance 7/20 to 11/20 and collapsing mean completion tokens 427.4 to 121.5, on local-ai's unported Python contracts under local-ai's own harness. Across harnesses the effect nulls, because mcgyvr's render_user_message already contains the rule — so the control as commissioned is the ablation, not a replay. Recovery is directional with the mechanism's signature: the rule's presence should raise acceptance materially and collapse completion tokens.
norule.note: It removes the section from the rendered message and changes nothing about output_schema, so the reply is parsed exactly as it is under the baseline. Ablating the schema instead would move the parser too, and the contrast would no longer be about the sentence.

cells.what: The code the scaffold saved, holding its plan fixed.
The scaffold entire — code and plan together.
#231 check 2. The output-shape rule's own contribution.

The first multi-lever cell, and the interaction term's first subject: whether the output-shape rule is worth more or less when the scaffold's code is gone. Two levers writing different slots, so the cell is order-independent.
